item: The custody and annotation Ed25519 keys are wrapped under the held passphrase like the evidence key; a key written before is wrapped in place, the same key (R449, R454)
key_paths: src/custody/keyfile.py; src/custody/signing.py; src/reporting/evidence.py; src/api/unlock.py; tests/test_custody_key_wrap.py; tests/test_shared_file_writes.py; docs/SECURITY.md; docs/USER_MANUAL.md
summary: On an install with a passphrase held (OO_KEY_PASSPHRASE, else the database passphrase) keys/custody_ed25519.pem, and the annotation signer's own keys/annotations_ed25519.pem (a distinct key, same HybridSigner code), are the custody signer's own wrap (scrypt N=2^15, AES-256-GCM) of the 32 raw key bytes, 76 bytes and not a PEM; before, they were PKCS8 under BestAvailableEncryption (PBKDF2 at 2048 rounds: 0.3 ms a guess against about 173 ms for the database the same passphrase protects, a cheap oracle for that passphrase). Without a passphrase the file stays a plaintext PKCS8 PEM. A key written before (plaintext or PKCS8) is wrapped IN PLACE the first time it is loaded under a passphrase: the same key, read back and compared before it replaces anything, so everything already signed still verifies; a PKCS8 file that could not be re-wrapped reads key_protection pkcs8-pbkdf2 rather than claiming the wrap. A new key is created 0600 from its first byte through a private copy under keys/.pending/ hard-linked into place, so two first callers end with one key; a symbolic link or a hard link outside keys/.pending/ at the key path is refused (KeyFileLinked), never wrapped by swapping the link. The create and replace-in-place protocol of #1749 moved out of src/reporting/evidence.py into src/custody/keyfile.py and now serves both signers (evidence.py is 217 lines shorter). parse_ed25519_key, seal_ed25519_key, parse_mldsa_key and seal_mldsa_key in src/custody/signing.py are public and read no environment and no held passphrase (the backup restore re-wraps through them, R448). COST, measured on 4 cores: every HybridSigner() under a passphrase now costs one scrypt, 79.2 ms and 32 MiB (0.33 ms before; twice that on a build with the ML-DSA library); callers are the four custody log routes, /api/custody/settings (the network consent popup), one CustodyLog per ingest batch, claim_bundle.py and annotation_signer(); a 50-way parallel construction is bounded to one derivation per core (_KDF_SLOTS: +1,298 MiB became +129 MiB). Not cached: a cache keyed on anything derived from the passphrase is a second place its consequences live. A build from before this change cannot read a key wrapped by it. Left, named: ML-DSA key creation (write_bytes then chmod) and a legacy plaintext ML-DSA key, the Set OO_KEY_PASSPHRASE hover in src/static/app-ai-tools.js (wrong advice for pkcs8-pbkdf2; a src/static change carries the 12-locale cost), keys_destroyed in src/safety/crypto_erase.py, a restore from an install with another passphrase (the custody routes refuse with the cause until the file is moved aside), and a real FAT/exFAT volume and Windows hard link, which are not measured.
